questions.q: Which palette type suits a variable that goes above and below a meaningful center, such as year-over-year change?
options: Categorical
Sequential
Rainbow
Diverging
questions.explain: A diverging palette uses two hues that meet at a neutral middle, so values above and below the center are easy to tell apart.

questions.q: Why should you avoid relying on red versus green alone to distinguish groups?
options: Red and green are too bright to print
matplotlib cannot draw red or green
Some readers have red-green color-vision deficiency, so they cannot tell the two apart
Red and green are always sequential colors
questions.explain: Roughly one in twelve men has some form of red-green color blindness. Use colorblind-safe palettes and add a second cue such as labels or markers.

questions.q: Which chart title follows this lesson's advice?
options: Average spend by region
West customers spend the most
Figure 1
Bar chart of the region column
questions.explain: A good title states the finding so the reader knows what to look for, instead of merely naming the topic.

questions.q: What is the 'grey everything, highlight one thing' technique?
options: Convert the whole chart to grayscale for printing
Use a rainbow palette so every bar stands out
Add a grey background behind the legend
Draw most data in a quiet grey and use one accent color for the item you want noticed
questions.explain: Muting everything except the point you are making directs the reader's attention where you want it.

questions.q: In the lesson's code, what does ax.bar_label(ax.containers[0], fmt="%.0f", padding=3) do?
options: Writes each bar's value on the chart as a direct label
Removes the bars from the chart
Sorts the bars from largest to smallest
Changes the palette to colorblind-safe colors
questions.explain: bar_label adds a value label to each bar; fmt controls the number format and padding sets the gap from the bar end.
